source_evidence: Many indexed annuities would consider 4.5% to be the index’s return when calculating any gains to your indexed annuity (7% - 2.5% = 4.5%).
answer: An indexed annuity’s return may be linked to a market index without including all of the index’s return. In particular, dividends paid by the securities in the index are generally excluded when calculating gains. For example, if an index’s total return is 7% and 2.5 percentage points came from dividends, an annuity might use 4.5% as the index return for its gain calculation. This means the annuity’s return can differ from the index’s total return.
